disease_label_per_paper: Scleroderma renal crisis in a normotensive patient
presentation_summary: A 34-year-old man developed systemic sclerosis features over about 6 months, including rash, arthralgia, myositis, dysphagia, weight loss, skin thickening of the hands, and positive anti-topoisomerase I antibody.

After prednisone 60 mg daily and methotrexate were prescribed, creatinine rose from 0.7 to 2.2 mg/dL within one week; two weeks later he presented with worsening shortness of breath, dysphagia, and hemoptysis while taking prednisone 40 mg daily.
Presentation blood pressure was 129/84 mmHg, above his approximate baseline of 100/60 mmHg but not frankly hypertensive; pulse was 99 bpm.

Admission labs showed hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, platelet count 29 x10^9/L, haptoglobin <8 mg/dL, creatinine 6.2 mg/dL, BUN 116 mg/dL, total bilirubin 5.5 mg/dL, indirect bilirubin 1.8 mg/dL, LDH 10461 U/L, and many schistocytes.
Urine microscopy showed dysmorphic RBCs and numerous granular casts; echocardiography showed EF 35%, and chest radiograph showed an equivocal left lower lobe opacity.
He was treated with captopril, plasma exchange, and hemodialysis. Kidney biopsy showed severe TMA with predominant vascular involvement and ischemic glomerular changes, supporting SRC.

He initially left hospital on enalapril, mycophenolate, and hemodialysis. Dialysis was later stopped when creatinine was 3.25 mg/dL with 24-hour creatinine clearance 26 mL/min, but he was rehospitalized with hypotension and severe cardiomyopathy and died after cardiac arrest.

quality_warnings: Renal biopsy, ADAMTS13, antiphospholipid testing, anti-GBM testing, and final paper diagnosis are retained as diagnostic/context evidence rather than presentation-only diagnosis labels.
Normotensive presentation is represented by absolute BP and transparent baseline delta; no hypertension value was invented.
No oxygen saturation was reported at this presentation, so none was structured.
